A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe AutoSERL and include Appendices A and B. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that pages 2–19 are identical; differences are confined to first-page author information and version metadata.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-world robot experiments across six manipulation tasks, including success rates, training times, robustness tests, and ablations in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original robot experiments and their numerical and graphical results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same sliding-window intervention, safety recovery, and intervention termination procedures. The training framework in Appendix A is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six insertion, hanging, and drawer-opening tasks on Franka and UR5 robots, including the same positional-variation scenario for plug insertion.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: SERL in Table 1, HIL-SERL in Table 2, and BC and MILES in Table 3. The graphical comparisons likewise retain the same methods.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same training budgets, demonstration counts, randomization settings, 300-step episode limit, and 50-episode evaluations with interventions disabled. Appendix task settings are identical.

E4.justification: Sections 4.3–4.6 retain identical robustness tests, heuristic-parameter sensitivity studies, component ablations, and demonstration-versus-policy trajectory analysis.

E5.justification: The five-seed plug-insertion experiment using seeds 40–44 and its curves and summary statistics in Figure 6(a) are unchanged. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or removed.

E6.justification: All result entries and plots are identical, including AutoSERL's 50/50 successes across six tasks, the baseline scores and training times in Tables 1–3, and the trajectory-length comparison of 99 versus 54 steps.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation in Section 3.1 and mathematical conditions defining intervention behavior are unchanged. Neither version adds distinct theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about automating intervention from one demonstration, outperforming the stated baselines, and matching HIL-SERL across the evaluated tasks.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are identical. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning diverse failure modes, single-trajectory recovery, and the 6D action space.

D1.justification: Hardware, implementation details, hyperparameters, action scales, and task ranges remain identical, including Appendices A–B and Tables A.1–A.3. The project website and code/video availability statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 29 references and identical related-work discussion and research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds corresponding-author markers and email addresses for Junge Zhang and Yaodong Yang alongside Ceyao Zhang, pluralizes the correspondence note, and updates the arXiv version/date. Scientific prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer correspondence footnote causes slight first-page text and spacing adjustments. All figures, tables, and layouts on pages 2–19 remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 updates corresponding-author attribution and contact information, with minor first-page reflow. The scientific content, empirical support, explanations, and reproducibility information, including both appendices, are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
